=== 5211: Mirror Hands ===

Let n be the number of players (3 or 4). Every player receives an identical hand of 14 cards: the colours Red, Blue, Green and Yellow, each with values 1 to 3 (written R1..R3, B1..B3, G1..G3, Y1..Y3), plus 2 Kododo cards (K), which have no colour and are worth 3 each. Hands are private, but because every hand starts identical and all played cards are revealed, anyone can track what each player has left. Each player is secretly dealt a bonus colour at random from Red, Blue, Green and Yellow, with no two players sharing one; only that player knows it. Scores and scored-card counts start at 0.

The game lasts 7 rounds. Each round:
1. Talk: every player writes one short message at the same time, without seeing the others; all messages are then shown to everyone. Nothing said is binding.
2. First card: every player at the same time places one card from their hand face down. 3. All first cards are revealed.
4. Second card: every player at the same time places one more card from their remaining hand face down. 5. All second cards are revealed. Played cards leave the hands.
6. Count K, the number of Kododos played this round, and how many cards of each colour were played.
7. Kododo check: if K equals exactly n-1 (2 with 3 players, 3 with 4 players), each player scores 3 points per Kododo they played this round and adds that many cards to their scored-card count, and no colour scores this round. If K is not exactly n-1, Kododos played this round score nothing and the colour check is made.
8. Colour check: a colour is busted if its count is n+1 or more (4+ with 3 players, 5+ with 4 players) and cannot score. Among colours that are not busted and were played at least once, find the highest count. If exactly one colour has it, that colour scores: each player scores the face values of their cards of that colour, plus 1 extra point per such card if it is their bonus colour, and adds those cards to their scored-card count. If two or more colours share the highest count, or no colour qualifies, nothing scores this round.
9. The round result and updated scores are announced.

After round 7 all cards have been played and the game ends. The highest total score wins; among players tied on score, the higher scored-card count wins; players still tied share the win.

Each player is secretly dealt a bonus colour at random from Red, Blue, Green and Yellow, with no two players sharing one; only that player knows it. Scores and scored-card counts start at 0.

The game lasts 7 rounds. Each round:
1. Talk: every player writes one short message at the same time, without seeing the others; all messages are then shown to everyone. Nothing said is binding.
2. First card: every player at the same time places one card from their hand face down. 3. All first cards are revealed.

6. Count K, the number of Kododos played this round, and how many cards of each colour were played.

Kododo check: if K equals exactly n-1 (2 with 3 players, 3 with 4 players), each player scores 3 points per Kododo they played this round and adds that many cards to their scored-card count, and no colour scores this round. If two or more colours share the highest count, or no colour qualifies, nothing scores this round.

records.system:
You are reviewing a game that has finished. You were not a player. You are shown everything: the messages the table was told, every move, and each player's private thinking at every move, which no other player ever saw. Each move carries the notes its game asked for, under their own names. The usual ones are:

  plan     what they meant to do over the coming turns
  reason   why they made that move
  predict  what they expected their opponents to do
  adjust   how they changed their own strategy because of that

Write two things.

First, a summary of the whole game as it unfolded: the turning points, the moves that decided it, and how it ended. Concrete: name seats, rounds and numbers.

Second, a review of each player. Judge their play, not their luck. For each one, compare their predictions with what their opponents were actually thinking and actually did: were they right, and did they see it in time? Did their adjustments follow from their predictions, and did their moves follow from their reasons? Point out their best and worst moves. Then score their play from 1 to 10, where 1 is aimless or self-defeating and 10 is sharp, well read and well executed. A player can lose and still score well, or win and score badly.

A player who gave no reasons, predictions or adjustments is judged on their moves alone; say that their thinking was not recorded.

Refer to each player by seat, and as "they".

THE GAME
Let n be the number of players (3 or 4). Every player receives an identical hand of 14 cards: the colours Red, Blue, Green and Yellow, each with values 1 to 3 (written R1..R3, B1..B3, G1..G3, Y1..Y3), plus 2 Kododo cards (K), which have no colour and are worth 3 each. Hands are private, but because every hand starts identical and all played cards are revealed, anyone can track what each player has left. Each player is secretly dealt a bonus colour at random from Red, Blue, Green and Yellow, with no two players sharing one; only that player knows it. Scores and scored-card counts start at 0.

The game lasts 7 rounds. Each round:
1. Talk: every player writes one short message at the same time, without seeing the others; all messages are then shown to everyone. Nothing said is binding.
2. First card: every player at the same time places one card from their hand face down. 3. All first cards are revealed.
4. Second card: every player at the same time places one more card from their remaining hand face down. 5. All second cards are revealed. Played cards leave the hands.
6. Count K, the number of Kododos played this round, and how many cards of each colour were played.
7. Kododo check: if K equals exactly n-1 (2 with 3 players, 3 with 4 players), each player scores 3 points per Kododo they played this round and adds that many cards to their scored-card count, and no colour scores this round. If K is not exactly n-1, Kododos played this round score nothing and the colour check is made.
8. Colour check: a colour is busted if its count is n+1 or more (4+ with 3 players, 5+ with 4 players) and cannot score. Among colours that are not busted and were played at least once, find the highest count. If exactly one colour has it, that colour scores: each player scores the face values of their cards of that colour, plus 1 extra point per such card if it is their bonus colour, and adds those cards to their scored-card count. If two or more colours share the highest count, or no colour qualifies, nothing scores this round.
9. The round result and updated scores are announced.

After round 7 all cards have been played and the game ends. The highest total score wins; among players tied on score, the higher scored-card count wins; players still tied share the win.
